elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both Parties.
elements.evidence: Section b) limits “the total liability for either Party,” making the cap mutual.

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap includes amounts paid or payable.
elements.evidence: The cap expressly uses “amounts paid or payable by IBM to MSL under this Agreement.”

elements.element: The fee-based limb uses a twelve-month measurement period.
elements.evidence: The clause specifies “the twelve (12) months immediately preceding” the relevant trigger.

elements.element: The twelve-month measurement period immediately precedes the claim.
elements.evidence: The period precedes “the event giving rise to the action,” not the claim. Those triggers can occur at different times.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the twelve-month fee amount and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The cap is expressly the greater of the paid-or-payable amount and US$1,000,000.

elements.element: Indirect damages are mutually excluded.
elements.evidence: Section a) excludes lost profits, consequential, punitive and incidental damages, but does not expressly exclude indirect damages.

elements.element: Consequential damages are mutually excluded.
elements.evidence: Section a) states that neither Party is liable to the other for consequential damages.

elements.element: Either Party's breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A Party’s breach of its confidentiality obligations is an Excluded Claim, and Excluded Claims are not subject to the cap.

elements.element: Either Party's breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: There is no carve-out for breach of data protection obligations.

elements.element: Either Party's breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: There is no carve-out for breach of security obligations.

elements.element: Either Party's indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: A Party’s indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims and are expressly not subject to the cap.

elements.element: Either Party's gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is included in the mutual definition of Excluded Claims and is not subject to the cap.

elements.element: Either Party's wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Willful misconduct is included in the mutual definition of Excluded Claims and is not subject to the cap.

elements.element: Either Party's fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Fraud is included in the mutual definition of Excluded Claims and is not subject to the cap.

elements.element: Either Party's infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Infringement of the other Party’s intellectual property rights is an Excluded Claim and is not subject to the cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are not treated as capped damages.
elements.evidence: IBM’s obligation to pay amounts due for Products is expressly not subject to the liability limitation, achieving the required cap treatment.

elements.element: The cap uses a twelve-month fees measure.
elements.evidence: The cap includes amounts paid or payable during the twelve months preceding the stated trigger. The additional US$1,000,000 floor is the preferred enhancement and does not remove the twelve-month-fee limb.

elements.element: Either Party's indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: A Party’s indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims and are not subject to the cap.

elements.element: Either Party's breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A Party’s breach of its confidentiality obligations is an Excluded Claim and is not subject to the cap.

elements.evidence: Gross negligence is an Excluded Claim and is not subject to the cap.

elements.element: Either Party's wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Willful misconduct is an Excluded Claim and is not subject to the cap.

result.reason: The redline satisfies the fallback because it provides a mutual cap incorporating a twelve-month fees measure and all four required fallback carve-outs. It does not satisfy the preferred position because indirect damages are not expressly excluded, data protection and security breaches are not carved out, and the twelve-month lookback runs from the event giving rise to the action rather than the claim. It is not minimal relative to the completed fallback because it also adds the US$1 million floor and several preferred-only carve-outs, although those additions are related and do not disturb unrelated commercial terms.
